title.narrative: Support to WFP Humanitarian Air Services ensuring critical lifesaving assistance reaches hard-to-reach areas

description.narrative: ltpgtSomalia is facing increasing humanitarian needs amidst concerns of El Niño and the risk of increased flooding along the Juba and Shabelle rivers that could result in loss of lives, property, destruction of infrastructure and crops, as well as massive population displacement. Approximately, 1.2 million people are estimated to be at risk of flooding including 600,000 at risk of displacement. Coupled with the drought-induced food insecurity and malnutrition witnessed so far in 2023, millions of people need urgent humanitarian assistance, including 4.3 million food-insecure people and 1.5 million children under the age of five facing acute malnutrition until mid-2024.ltbrgtThe operating environment in Somalia remains very challenging. Regular and sustained access to the most affected areas has been hindered due to conflict, insecurity, and deteriorating infrastructure, thus hampering the ability of the humanitarian community to efficiently deliver humanitarian assistance to vulnerable populations. Road access continues to be challenging with about 90 per cent of primary roads requiring extensive rehabilitation. This in turn creates a heavy reliance on costly air services to access hard-to-reach locations. ltbrgtStocks are recurrently concentrated in major hubs, like Mogadishu, necessitating the use of air transport to reach the final destinations. Despite the numerous airstrips in flood-affected areas, especially within the Shabelle and Jubaland region, these airstrips are often directly impacted by flooding. In the event that these airstrips become inaccessible to fixed-wing aircraft due to heavy rain, helicopters become the primary mode of transport as they can land on smaller landing areas and, at times, on softer ground, allowing access to these otherwise isolated areas. However, helicopters come with limitations in cargo capacity and higher operational costs, making it challenging for the humanitarian community, especially for smaller non-governmental organizations, to access these services. ltbrgtWith ongoing support from the Somalia Logistics Cluster and the United Nations Humanitarian Air Service (UNHAS), the humanitarian community has been able to provide much-needed assistance across the country, but reduced funding threatens to stop the provision of this critical service. This is particularly critical as the anticipated El Nino is expected to cause increased flooding thus making access extremely difficult.ltbrgtlt/pgt
